Morphemes can be divided into (1) those hav- ing a variable and (2) those having a fixed tone/ aspect structure. The former change their tone and aspect behaviour according to the context in which they occur, the latter have identical tone/ aspect shapes in all environments. Type (1) morphemes include noun and verb stems. new_statements.rule_in_words: Heine analyses Elmolo with three tones (High, Low, Falling) plus a separately recorded 'accent' that has no fixed position: it usually, but not always, sits on a high-toned syllable. Tone/accent patterns of noun and verb stems vary with grammatical context (e.g. the verb 'go' appears with High, Falling, Low, or 'Falling + Accent' patterns in different TAM forms), while certain affixes (Person-Aspect prefixes) fix the tone and accent of the following syllable. No positional (initial/penult/final) word-stress rule is given.
new_statements.exceptions: Accent occurs on high-tone syllables 'in most, though not in all, cases'; a footnote notes a falling tone appears 'if followed by one syllable only (see 2.63)'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tone and accent marking in a short sketch based on 1970s fieldwork with the last (per Sasse 1992, 'rusty') speakers; accent interacts with verbal morphology (grammatical tone/accent). Only the OpenLibrary/IA search-API fragments of the page were obtainable (full scan is lending-restricted), so the quote is stitched from overlapping verbatim fragments; wording of the deciding sentence is complete across two overlapping fragments.
new_statements.identity_note: Heine 1980 describes the original Cushitic (Western Omo-Tana) Elmolo = Glottolog elmo1238, recorded in the 1970s from the last, already Samburu-dominant speakers (Sasse 1992 apud Tosco 2015: 'rusty speakers'); the language is now extinct/remembered only as isolated words. It must not be confused with 'Elmolo-Samburu', the Maa (Samburu, samb1315) variety the El Molo speak today (Brenzinger 1992), nor with the Camus (Il-Chamus, Maa) chapter of the same book, whose sec. 2.14 'Note on accent' gives positional accent rules that are NOT about Elmolo.
